items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: there are about a dozen people who wrote articles, some of them reprints like Charles Smith and Danny Barker and people of that kind

ctx.x: Weren't there corrections made though, and then charged against the money?

Well, I don't know whether they could have been charged. They might have been charged. There was no, the first royalty was all used up anyway with the free copies that we had to give away. See, books like this, everybody wants copies of it. That's one reason I figured the Jelly Roll book, I'd better wait a few years until everybody's dead. I've promised so many copies. I've had over sixty interviews, and there are about a dozen people who wrote articles, some of them reprints like Charles Smith and Danny Barker…
You could go to Preservation Hall and sell a thousand a night. Just sign your name on them. I know Squibb once said, they have orders for about four hundred from libraries.

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-09-04
items.q: So Charles had supervised and arranged the sessions, so he arranged with this tempo magazine that I review the album.

ctx.x: He received you very ambly, though.

Yeah, very friendly. When Jelly, you see, there was that seniority business, too, that he wouldn't have, Judy, being younger, wouldn't have dared be leader. Once they wanted Jelly to record with Victor, I mean, with Decca, with Louis Armstrong, is what I'm trying to say, when they made that new Arlene's album that Louis made, and Steve Smith also organized that date. The same one that Judy was in, had a band, and the one where they makes the 219 blues. Sidney Bechet was on the date, too. And Jelly was supposed to…
Which place is that now? Music Box. The same place here.
